places.name: Bích Khê Trấn
places.size: A small walled jade-trade town of about 1,100 roofs inside a wall about 450 m by 320 m, roughly 5,000 people, on a brook whose stepped weirs run about 2 km; carvers' workshops along the main street.
places.where: Region 1, northern road country of Thiên Xu, temperate forest at about 80 m. On the map a forested valley with a thin blue brook winding down in sharp angles from the top left to the lower right, golden-green meadows and a grey rocky ridge at the left edge. Thiên Xu Tông town, Wood and Water. Nearest: Khê Sam Lâm forest 75 km, Thiết Đề Nguyên beast lair 150 km. Named for the jade-green brook around 300.
places.imagined: Late afternoon on a brook so green it looks dyed. Jade-pickers kneel on the shallow stone weirs sorting pebbles into baskets by colour, and the polishing wheels hum in the workshops along the main street.
places.subject: The place: Bích Khê Trấn, the Jade Brook town, a small walled town of jade pickers and carvers. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a forested valley of dark green conifer and golden-green meadow fills the frame, a grey rocky ridge at the left edge, and a thin brook of vivid jade-green water winding in sharp angles from the upper left down to the lower right and passing beside the town. The town: a low town of about eleven hundred grey-tile roofs inside a small rectangular wall about four hundred and fifty metres long, one gate tower at the road and one at the brook, a main street running between them lined with long workshops whose roofs have rows of skylights, a small market square, a stone guildhall of jade dealers with a deep roof, courtyard houses and drying yards for polished stone; chimneys of the wheel-houses leak thin smoke. Signature element: below the walls the brook is stepped by about a dozen shallow stone weirs, each a low pale curved dam, so that the vivid jade-green water spills in a staircase of bright green ribbons across the meadow, and on every weir tiny pickers kneel in rows sorting pebbles into baskets set out by colour, pale green, deep green, white, in neat rows on the bank. Baskets and small workshops edge the bank; forest and ridges rise beyond. Life at scale: carters on the road with crates of seals, a bride's party carrying an uncut pebble in a red cloth, children skipping stones. Light and season: late afternoon in early autumn, warm golden light from the upper left making the green water glow, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Thanh Bách Thành
places.size: A walled city on the northern road of about 15,000 roofs and perhaps 75,000 people, walls about 2.6 km by 1.9 km, with a cypress in nearly every courtyard and a round crater pond about 150 m across outside the north wall; an ore-cart and officials' waystation.
places.where: Region 1/2, northern road, temperate forest at about 120 m. On the map rolling golden-green meadow and forest hills, a river winding down from the top left in sharp angles, orange-red barren earth at the lower right and a grey rocky ridge at the lower left. Thiên Xu Tông city founded 520. Nearest: Cổ Bách Lâm forest 75 km, Bạch Lộc Quán ruin 152 km. A star fell near the city in 980.
places.imagined: Dusk on the northern road. Dark narrow cypresses stand over every courtyard, ore carts and officials' carriages stream through the gates, and a small round crater pond outside the north wall shines black and glassy.
places.subject: The place: Thanh Bách Thành, the Green Cypress city, a walled waystation city on the northern road. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; rolling golden-green meadow and forest hills fill the frame, a river winding in sharp angles down from the upper left past the city's west side, a stretch of orange-red barren earth at the lower right and a grey rocky ridge at the lower left. The city: a great rectangular wall of grey stone about two and a half kilometres long with a tall three-storey gate tower the tallest roofline, enclosing some fifteen thousand grey-tile roofs in orderly blocks, and between the roofs hundreds of tall, narrow, dark-green cypresses, one in nearly every courtyard, so that the city looks stippled with dark exclamation marks; a wide main avenue running gate to gate, an officials' yamen with a big courtyard, ore-cart depots with long sheds and hundreds of parked carts, inns, a market square and a bell tower. Signature element: just outside the north wall lies a small round crater pond about a hundred and fifty metres across, black and glassy at its rim, still and mirror-like, the scar of a fallen star, with a ring of raised earth around it and a small path and a stone coin-toss platform at its edge. A road runs through the city from the north gate to the south gate, with a train of ore carts on it. Life at scale: carriages of officials with outriders, hundreds of tiny carters, townsfolk tossing coins at the pond. Light and season: dusk in early autumn, golden light from the upper left on the walls and the cypress tips, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Ba Quang Thôn
places.size: A fishing village of about 18 low houses with reed rafts and boats, perhaps 90 people, on a gravel shore about 250 m across beside a chain of about 5 small bright lakes stepping inland.
places.where: Region 1/2, grassland coast at about 90 m. On the map a deep blue sea bay at the upper right with a forested headland at upper left, a green coast and a river winding down at the lower middle, a rocky grey ridge at the lower right. A Cửu Cao Phái village, Water, Wood. Nearest: Kiêu Minh Lâm 112 km, Cựu Tân Trấn 141 km, Khai Dương Thành 190 km. Travellers have taken it for a fire since 600.
places.imagined: Midday blaze. The little lakes throw so much light that the village seems to stand in fire, flat reed rafts lie on the beach, and the elders squint.
places.subject: The place: Ba Quang Thôn, the Wave-Light village, a fishing village on a sea shore beside a chain of mirror-bright lakes. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a deep blue sea bay fills the upper right with white wave lines, a forested headland at the upper left, the green grassy coast sloping in the middle with a river winding down at the lower middle and a rocky grey ridge at the lower right. The village: about eighteen low houses of grey tile and reed roofs on the gravel shore, with fish racks, net-mending frames, and a small plank landing, a few boats drawn up on the gravel and flat reed rafts laid out in rows on the beach ready for the evening nets, a small shrine with a single roof. Signature element: behind the village a chain of about five small bright lakes steps down the grassy slope toward the sea, each lake a round or oval sheet of mirror water about eighty to two hundred metres across, each throwing back the sunlight as a blinding disc of gold, so that the whole slope behind the village seems to blaze; narrow grass dykes and reed margins separate them. Life at scale: villagers squinting under hands, children wading with spears for small fish, a crane rider's mount landing by the lakes, two tiny ferrymen poling a raft. Light and season: midday in summer, strong golden light from the upper left, the lakes dazzling white-gold, short crisp shadows under the rafts and houses toward the lower right.

places.name: Hạc Quy Thôn
places.size: A marsh-edge village of about 25 reed-thatched and grey-tile houses with a crescent landing pool about 80 m long, perhaps 120 people, in about 300 m.
places.where: Region 1/2, slow river at a marsh edge, temperate forest at about 70 m. On the map dark green forest with a river winding in sharp angles from the top to the lower middle, golden meadow at the lower left, a grey rocky outcrop at lower left. Thiên Xu village by Cửu Cao Phái's cranes. Nearest: Hạc Tức Mạch 75 km, Khê Sam Lâm 146 km. Cranes return here on the same day every year.
places.imagined: Landing day. The whole village stands silent around the crescent pool edged with flat grey stones while the first cranes come down out of the sky.
places.subject: The place: Hạc Quy Thôn, the Crane Homecoming village, a quiet marsh-edge village on a slow river. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; dark green forest fills the right of frame, a slow river winding in sharp angles from the top to the lower middle with green reed banks, a golden meadow at the lower left and a grey rocky outcrop at the left edge, still marsh pools among the reeds. The village: about twenty-five reed-thatched and grey-tile houses along the river bank in a loose line with small yards, drying racks for reeds, a few punts on the water, a modest village hall with a larger roof and a stone-edged well. Signature element: in the green meadow beyond the houses a crescent-shaped landing pool, about eighty metres long, is dug in the turf and edged with flat grey stepping stones, its water clear and weed-free, the crescent's horns pointing toward the river; around it the grass is cut short, and about forty tiny villagers stand in a silent ring at its edge, while the first dozen white cranes come down from the sky with legs trailing and wings spread, two of them already standing in the pool, and a handful of crane riders' mounts among them. Life at scale: a mother lifting a child to see, an old man with a staff, a boy clearing the last weed by hand, a few ducks. Light and season: golden morning in early spring, light from the upper left on the white birds and the grey stones, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Lộc Uyển Thôn
places.size: A hillside village of about 15 log houses above a high meadow about 500 m across, perhaps 75 people; a black stele about 3 m tall and a heap of shed antlers; the herd of about 100 deer is the larger presence.
places.where: Region 1/2, hill country of the northern road, temperate forest at about 100 m. On the map golden meadows and dark forest ridges with a river winding in sharp angles from the top left to the lower right. Thiên Xu village. Nearest: Lão Du Lâm 75 km, Bạch Lộc Quán ruin 127 km, Cổ Bách Lâm 141 km. Deer have gathered each spring since before 380, when Thiên Xu forbade hunting there.
places.imagined: A spring dawn. Hundreds of deer graze the high meadow, a black stele stands at its edge with a heap of pale shed antlers at its foot, and children are laying more antlers as a gift to the Pivot.
places.subject: The place: Lộc Uyển Thôn, the Deer Park village, a hillside village above a high meadow where deer gather. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; golden meadow slopes and dark forest ridges fill the frame, a river winding in sharp angles from the upper left to the lower right, a stream running down beside the village, and a rail fence along the slope. The village: about fifteen log houses with grey-tile roofs on a forested slope, in a loose row following a path, each with a woodpile, a goat pen and a small kitchen plot, smoke from three chimneys. Beneath them lies a high green meadow about five hundred metres across, and a rail fence keeps the village goats off the deer's grass. Signature element: at the meadow's edge stands a black stone stele three metres tall with its face blank, the hunting ban, with a great heap of pale shed antlers around its foot, bone-white against the green; across the meadow about a hundred deer, tawny specks with antlers, graze in groups, with stags in a line at the far edge. The deer are pale gold in the low sun, and their breath hangs in small clouds over the grass. Life at scale: a group of children carrying antlers to the stele, an old herdsman with a staff at the fence, two tiny villagers pointing out a poacher's trail to a watcher. Light and season: spring dawn, golden light from the upper left on the meadow and the stele, long soft shadows toward the lower right, mist in the hollows.

places.name: Phụ Tinh Phong
places.size: A glacier peak at about 4.3 km altitude, about 6 km across at its base; on its broad shoulder a flat terrace cut into the ice about 400 m by 100 m with rows of about 200 rusted iron stakes; no buildings, no one.
places.where: Region 1/2, Dao Quang Lĩnh, glacier at about 4.3 km. On the map a mountain range of grey rock ridges with white snow along the crests, a blue bay at the top and a river winding at the lower left, forest in the left valley. Peak beside taller neighbours, belongs to no sect. Nearest: Quan Triều Phong 112 km. Phá Quân Môn's disciples drilled here at night under the faint companion star.
places.imagined: A cold clear dusk. White ice over dark rock, a flat terrace on the broad shoulder bristling with rusted iron stakes where weapon racks stood, the wind singing over them, and one faint star above the summit.
places.subject: The place: Phụ Tinh Phong, the Companion Star Peak, a glacier peak with an abandoned drill terrace. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a sharp glacier peak stands in the centre of the frame among a range of grey rock ridges, white ice and blue shadow over dark rock, snow lying along the crests and in the gullies, a blue bay at the top right of the frame, a thin river and green forest valley at the left. A broad shoulder below the summit has been cut into a flat terrace, about four hundred metres long and a hundred wide, benched into the ice; across it stand rows of about two hundred tiny rust-red iron stakes, in regular ranks, the remains of weapon racks, each casting a thin shadow, with a faint dusting of snow between the ranks and drifts piled against the windward side. A pale path of old footsteps leads from a ridge below to the terrace; a few stakes lean or have fallen. Beside the peak, taller neighbours rise out of drifting cloud. A faint pale star-glint hangs above the summit. No buildings, no huts; no one drills here now. The ice below the terrace is crossed by deep blue crevasses, and wind has carved the snow into long smooth ripples. Life at scale: one tiny figure of a Thiên Xu patrol standing at the terrace's edge. Light and season: cold clear dusk in autumn, golden light from the upper left on the ice and the rust-red stakes, long soft blue shadows toward the lower right, a few clouds below.

places.name: Trích Tinh Phong
places.size: The roof of the heartland: a dark rock peak 4.7 km high, about 8 km across at its foot, with a stone needle summit and a pilgrims' stair of about 1,000 rock-cut steps on its ridge spine; no buildings but a few tiny waystation huts.
places.where: Region 1/2, Dao Quang Lĩnh high mountains. On the map a huge grey and white range of ridges and snow, a river from the upper left, orange-brown moorland at the left and a small blue tarn at the lower middle. Belongs to no sect. Nearest: Tuyết Ngọc Khoáng 79 km, Phá Quân Môn 125 km, Ngân Giáp Phong 146 km. Watchmen climbed it in 260 and said one could pluck the stars by hand.
places.imagined: Clear dusk above the clouds. A thin stone needle ends the summit, strips of white cloth tied round it stream in the wind, and a thread of stair runs up the ridge spine from the collar of cloud.
places.subject: The place: Trích Tinh Phong, the Star-Plucking Peak, the roof of the heartland. Setting: seen from very high above at a steep aerial angle; a vast range of grey rock ridges and white snowfields fills the frame, running from the upper right to the lower left in parallel folds, a dark rock peak rising in the centre clear of a collar of cloud, snow in the gullies, orange-brown moorland at the left, a small blue tarn near the lower middle, a river at the top left. The summit ends in a thin stone needle, a few tens of metres of bare rock, wrapped with dozens of strips of white cloth that stream in the wind like pale flames. Signature element: up the ridge spine below the needle runs a pilgrims' road of about a thousand rock-cut steps, a thin pale thread zigzagging up the crest, and at its beginning a faint line of tiny dark dots, pilgrims climbing in single file; at three places along it, tiny stone waystation huts with grey roofs show as dots. Clouds fill the valleys below, so the peak looks like an island above a white sea. Life at scale: about a dozen pilgrims in single file, one at the needle tying a strip. Light and season: clear cold dusk in autumn, golden light from the upper left gilding the needle and the white cloth, deep blue shadows lying across the ridges toward the lower right, the first stars faintly visible in the dark sky above.

places.name: Tinh Tủy Mạch
places.size: A black rock face about 600 m high carrying seams of star marrow, with a ledge holding a low curved stone breastwork about 30 m long, a guards' fire pit and a tiny hut; a guard of about 20 men; no settlement.
places.where: Region 1/2, high in Dao Quang Lĩnh at about 3 km. On the map a huge grey and white range of jagged ridges and snow with a dark volcanic-looking crater at the top and small green strips in the valleys, a river at the lower left. Wild spirit vein (Metal, Earth), held by Thiên Xu Tông, 4 tiles from Băng Tâm's border. Nearest: Hàn Tinh Phong 90 km, Ẩn Tinh Phong 100 km.
places.imagined: Noon on a black face. Seams of silver-white star marrow glitter like frost, a low breastwork and a guards' fire pit stand on the ledge, and cranes wheel over it in slow rings.
places.subject: The place: Tinh Tủy Mạch, the Star Marrow Vein, a guarded vein of star marrow high on a black rock face. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a huge range of jagged grey and white ridges and snowfields fills the frame, a dark crater-like hollow at the top, strips of green forest in the valleys at the left and a river at the lower left, brown moorland at the lower right. In the middle a black high-mountain rock face rises in steep rock ribs, seamed with bright silver-white glittering veins that thread through the stone like frost, some as wide as a road, branching and rejoining across the whole face, flashing at noon. Signature element: the glittering silver-white veins on the black face, the brightest thing in the frame. On a ledge before the face stands a low curved stone breastwork about thirty metres long with a tiny glowing fire pit at its centre and a small grey hut; a narrow guarded path zigzags in from the right. Snowfields above, and tiny white crane specks, about a dozen, circling in slow rings over the face. Frost fringes every rib of black rock, and the fire pit's smoke goes straight up in the still air. Life at scale: five tiny guards at the breastwork, one on watch with a spear, one adding fuel to the fire pit. Light and season: clear noon in early winter, strong golden light from the upper left making the veins flash, deep blue shadows in the ribs, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Phá Quân Môn
places.size: The ruined mountain fort of a vassal sect that rebelled and was destroyed in 874: about 60 burned buildings and a wall about 300 m long on a high shoulder; once a few hundred, now empty; miners of the range pass it.
places.where: Region 1/2, high mountain shoulder at about 2.9 km, Dao Quang Lĩnh. On the map a huge range of grey and white ridges and snow, a blue lake at the lower right, orange-brown moorland at the left and green pockets on the slopes. Former sect, held by Thiên Xu Tông. Nearest: Bạch Tích Khoáng 106 km, Lô Cam Khoáng 112 km, Trích Tinh Phong 125 km. Hạ Lang Tinh led it against its lord and Thiên Xu destroyed it in 874.
places.imagined: A grey cold afternoon. A stone gate arch split clean down the middle still stands, its halves leaning apart, seven iron star-studs on the broken lintel, and grass grows in the old parade ground.
places.subject: The place: Phá Quân Môn, the Army-Breaker Gate, the ruined mountain fort of a rebel sect. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a high mountain shoulder of grey rock and brown scree fills the frame in a country of white-capped ridges, orange-brown moorland at the left, green pockets along the slopes, a blue lake at the lower right. The ruin: a rectangle of fire-blackened wall stubs about three hundred metres long climbing the shoulder, about sixty burned buildings, barracks lines and a long drill hall with no roof, the stump of a watchtower cut off at half height, a ruined armoury, the parade ground overgrown with grass and with the outline of old drill squares still visible as paler rectangles. Signature element: a stone gate arch about ten metres tall is split clean down the middle, its two halves leaning away from each other, a row of seven small iron studs in the shape of the Dipper running across its broken lintel, and the pale road leading to it passes between the halves. The place is scorched and silent: soot-black stone against the pale grass. Wiry grass has grown through the burned floors, and the hillside road is rutted by old carts. Life at scale: no one lives here; two tiny miners with picks walking past on the lower path, a single hawk. Light and season: cold grey late afternoon in autumn, thin golden light from the upper left on the arch and the scorched stone, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Bằng Sào Nhai
places.size: A sheer pale cliff about 500 m high and about 3 km long with a nest about 30 m across of whole bleached pine trunks on a ledge near its top; no buildings; the roc's feathers lie in the scree below.
places.where: Region 1/2, highland at about 1.5 km, Dao Quang Lĩnh. On the map a pale grey and rust-orange highland of broken rock with small tarns, grassland at the lower left and dark forest at the lower right. Beast lair, a roc (yêu cốt prize), belonging to no sect. Nearest: Lộc Giác Phong 125 km, Thạch Cổ Phong 127 km. Cửu Cao's riders fly their cranes wide of the cliff.
places.imagined: A hard clear afternoon. A sheer pale cliff towers over the forest with a nest the size of a farmhouse on a ledge near the top, long feathers lying in the scree, and nothing else nests in sight.
places.subject: The place: Bằng Sào Nhai, the Roc's Nest Cliff, a sheer pale cliff with a gigantic nest. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a highland of pale grey rock and rust-orange broken ground fills the frame, small blue tarns scattered, grassland at the lower left and dark forest at the lower right. A sheer pale cliff of pale rock about five hundred metres high and three kilometres long runs across the middle, its face striped with vertical streaks of grey and cream, its foot in a long apron of scree and dark forest. Signature element: on a ledge near the top of the cliff sits a huge nest about thirty metres across woven from whole pine trunks bleached grey, the trunks as long as ships, stacked in a thick ring, with a deep hollow in its middle and a few shreds of bone and white down; it is the size of a farmhouse beside the cliff. In the scree below lie several feathers longer than a man, pale grey and white with dark tips, like fallen masts. Nothing else nests within sight; the scree is empty of birds. A great roc, a tiny dark winged shape with a wingspan the width of the nest, soars far off over the forest, its shadow crossing the foothills. No buildings; a tiny feather-gatherer climbs the scree. Light and season: hard clear afternoon in early autumn, golden light from the upper left on the cliff face and the nest, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Họa Tinh Đường
places.size: A hall of talisman painters, about 45 painters, ink-makers and fungus gatherers: a compound of about 35 grey-roofed buildings in forest within about 220 m, with soot kilns, ink grinding sheds and fungus beds; small and still, its painters sit so long that moths settle on them.
places.where: Region 1/2, northern pine forest of Dao Quang Lĩnh, temperate forest at about 90 m. On the map an unbroken carpet of dark green conifer forest with pale grassy ridges and a bright turquoise lake bay at the right edge and a pale rocky outcrop at the lower middle. Vassal of Thiên Xu Tông, Wood 51 %, Water 16 %. Nearest: Ngân Dương Lâm 177 km, Lâm Biên Thôn 225 km.
places.imagined: A still dusk. Painters sit before long drawing tables in an open hall, so motionless that moths have settled on their shoulders, while smoke from the soot kilns rises thin and straight behind.
places.subject: The place: Họa Tinh Đường, the Hall of the Painted Stars, a hall of talisman painters in northern pine forest. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; an unbroken carpet of dark green conifer forest fills the frame with pale grassy ridges running through it, a bright turquoise lake bay at the right edge, a pale rocky outcrop at the lower middle. The hall: in a clearing about two hundred metres across stands a compound of about thirty-five grey-tile buildings of pine timber around three courtyards, a gate hall, a very long painting hall with the whole south side open to a veranda so that rows of painters at low tables can be seen in lines, a drying loft with hundreds of talismans on cords like a field of pale flags with no marks, a cedar-roofed hall for the head, dormitories, a kitchen; behind them a row of six round soot kilns built of clay and set well apart from the trees, thin smoke rising, with a line of ink-grinding sheds and cakes of black ink drying on racks; and a long damp shed of fungus beds where gatherers lay out their harvest. Signature element: the painting hall's veranda with about forty painters sitting in perfectly still rows, so still that a few pale moths have settled on them, and the drying cords of blank pale talismans fluttering across the court in lines. Life at scale: a courier in Thiên Xu's grey collecting a box, fungus gatherers returning with baskets, a child grinding ink. Light and season: still dusk in late autumn, golden light from the upper left on the veranda, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Lê Hoa Am (the Gate Hermitage)
places.size: Now the Gate Hermitage, the old seat of a women-only ice hermitage (about 40 women in the sect, mainly the grey sisters here): about 25 small white-plastered halls on narrow terraces in a pear orchard of about 300 old trees, 400 m on a steep slope, a three-roof bell pagoda; small, white and quiet. The white nuns have moved up the glacier.
places.where: Region 7/southern massif, high mountain at about 680 m. On the map a steep ridge country of grey rock ribs with snowy crests and dark conifer and a green tongue running down at the upper middle, yellow-orange moorland at the right. Vassal of Băng Tâm Các, righteous, Metal 42 %, no Ice, which is why the seat moved to Lăng Tuyệt Phong. Nearest: Huyền Băng Phong 79 km, Tuyết Tôn Phong 125 km, Hàn Ngọc Khoáng mine 146 km. Founded 600 after a snow fell like pear blossom overnight.
places.imagined: A winter morning. An orchard of old pear trees white with rime looks like a hillside in full blossom, small white halls climb narrow terraces, and a three-roof bell pagoda rises over them.
places.subject: The place: Lê Hoa Am, the Pear Blossom Hermitage, here as the Gate Hermitage of an ice sect of women, on a steep snowy slope. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a steep ridge country of grey rock ribs, snowy crests and dark conifer fills the frame, a green tongue of forest running down at the upper middle, yellow-orange moorland at the right edge, the ground between the ridges dusted with snow. The hermitage: about twenty-five small white-plastered halls with grey-tile roofs on narrow terraces climbing a steep slope in a staggered line, linked by stone stairs and short covered galleries, a gate hall at the foot where visitors are met, a refectory, cells in rows, a herb garden under snow cloths, a bell pagoda of three roofs at the top, the tallest outline; behind them the white pagoda catches the sun. Signature element: all around the halls an orchard of about three hundred gnarled pear trees, their branches thick with white rime like blossom, so that from a distance the whole hillside looks in full bloom in the dead of winter; rime also coats the roof edges and the terrace walls. A few trees are cleared with long poles by tiny grey-clad figures. Life at scale: about a dozen tiny grey sisters sweeping the stairs and carrying firewood, two white-robed nuns at the pagoda, a pilgrim at the gate. Light and season: bright winter morning, golden light from the upper left on the rimed pear trees, long soft blue shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Hòe Âm Trấn
places.size: A small harbour town of about 1,000 roofs inside a wall about 400 m by 300 m, roughly 4,500 people, at a river mouth, with a quay about 200 m long and an avenue of about 120 old locust trees climbing 2 km toward the mountains.
places.where: Region 7, southern coast at sea level. On the map a deep blue sea bay at the upper left with a forested shore, a river winding down at the left and a rocky grey ridge at the right and lower left. Held by Lê Hoa Am. Nearest: Hào Trư Cương beast lair 90 km, Tầm Kiếm Đường 177 km, Hàn Khê Thôn 182 km. The Tiêu family planted the locusts around 520; a hunter found a sealed cave in 930.
places.imagined: Early summer. Fishing boats and the hermitage's supply carts share one narrow quay, locust blossom falls on the avenue, and the crowns meet overhead in a green tunnel that climbs toward the mountains.
places.subject: The place: Hòe Âm Trấn, the Locust Shade town, a small harbour town at a river mouth with an avenue of ancient locusts. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a deep blue bay fills the upper left with a forested shore, a river winding down at the left and meeting the sea beside the town, a rocky grey ridge at the right and lower left, with white surf on its coast. The town: a low harbour town of about a thousand grey-tile roofs inside a rectangular wall about four hundred metres long at the river mouth, one sea gate and one landward gate, narrow lanes, a fish market, drying yards, a single narrow stone quay about two hundred metres long where about thirty fishing boats and a few supply carts share the space, a timber wharf with crates for the hermitage up the mountain. Signature element: from the landward back gate an avenue of about a hundred and twenty ancient locust trees, in a double row with their crowns meeting overhead in a green tunnel, climbs uphill for two kilometres toward the mountains, a dark-green line against the paler slopes; in early summer pale blossom has dropped and lies like snow in a long strip along the road. Life at scale: ox carts with supplies winding up the avenue, hunters at the gate, fishermen hauling nets, children chasing blossom. Light and season: bright early summer morning, golden light from the upper left on the locust crowns and the boats, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Đỗ Quyên Thôn
places.size: A fishing village of about 18 low houses with dark stone-slab roofs, perhaps 90 people, on a grey shore in about 250 m; the azalea slope above covers about a square kilometre.
places.where: Region 7, far north coast at sea level, with temperate forest. On the map a bay of blue sea at the left and another at the upper right with a forested peninsula between them, a rocky grey ridge at the lower right. Băng Tâm Các village. Nearest: Hàn Sam Lâm 125 km, Hoàng Oanh Thôn 158 km. Azaleas are said to be the dead of the eruption of Chúc Long Sơn.
places.imagined: The first day of bloom. The whole steep slope is blood-red with azaleas above the low stone-roofed houses like a fire about to come down, the village leaves rice cakes at the foot of the slope and does not fish.
places.subject: The place: Đỗ Quyên Thôn, the Azalea village, a fishing village under a slope of red azaleas. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a peninsula of forested land runs from the top of the frame to the lower middle between two bays of grey-blue sea, a rocky grey ridge at the lower right, white surf along the black volcanic shore. The village: about eighteen low houses of dark stone with roofs of dark stone slabs weighted against the wind, in a loose double row along a grey shore, a black volcanic shingle beach with about fifteen small boats hauled up in a line, net racks and fish-drying frames, a landing of piled stones. Signature element: above the village a steep slope is blanketed in bright vermilion azalea blooms, about a square kilometre of crimson, the colour deepened by the golden light, running up to the dark forest edge, so that it looks like a fire about to come down on the roofs; at the slope's foot a flat stone shelf holds about thirty rice cakes in rows, small white dots, and a small cairn. No boat is out on the water; the fishers stand in a line at the foot of the slope. Life at scale: a hundred or so tiny villagers standing quietly at the stone shelf, children carrying cakes, smoke thin from two chimneys. Light and season: spring afternoon, warm golden light from the upper left deepening the red, long soft shadows toward the lower right, the sea grey.

places.name: Hoàng Oanh Thôn
places.size: A coastal-valley village of about 20 grey-tile houses in a ring, perhaps 100 people, in a valley about 300 m across; about 40 willows hung with about 150 woven straw bird shelters.
places.where: Region 7, far north coast, sheltered valley at sea level, temperate forest. On the map a wide bay of blue water at the left with a forested peninsula running down to the lower right, snow-streaked grey ridges at the lower right, another bay at the upper right. Băng Tâm Các village. Nearest: Dã Liễu Lâm forest 100 km, Đỗ Quyên Thôn 158 km. Orioles winter in the valley.
places.imagined: Midwinter. Bare willows hung with round woven straw bird shelters flash yellow with orioles, the only birdsong in the ice mountains, and snow lies on the ridges all around.
places.subject: The place: Hoàng Oanh Thôn, the Oriole village, a ring of houses among bare willows in a sheltered coastal valley. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a sheltered valley on the coast of a wide blue bay with a forested peninsula running down to the lower right, snow-streaked grey ridges at the lower right corner and snow lying on the ridges all round, another bay at the upper right. The village: a ring of about twenty low grey-tile houses with smoking chimneys around a small snow-dusted green with a well and a stone hearth, each house with a yard and woodpile, a short shingle beach with a few boats and net racks, a small plank landing. Signature element: around and among the houses about forty bare willow trees, each hung with a number of round woven straw bird shelters, about a hundred and fifty in all, little round baskets with an opening, each dotted with tiny yellow specks of orioles, so that the grey winter trees seem to bear yellow fruit; flickers of yellow in flight between them. The bay beyond the beach is pale grey-blue, and the willows' bare branches make a fine brown net against the snow. Life at scale: villagers weaving fresh shelters in a yard, children feeding birds with grain, two white-robed nuns come down from the mountain standing quietly under a tree to listen, smoke from chimneys. Light and season: clear midwinter late morning, golden light from the upper left on the yellow birds and the grey roofs, long soft blue shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Hồi Lộ Phong
places.size: A steep ice peak about 3.5 km high, about 5 km across at its base, wrapped in a switchback stair of carved ice steps about 2 km long with some 90 turns; no buildings.
places.where: Region 7, far north ice mountains. On the map a vast grey and white range of ridges and snowfields with a dark crater near the lower left of centre, a blue sea at the top left, a few strips of dark forest at the upper middle. Belongs to no sect. Nearest: Bão Tuyết Phong 103 km, Hàn Ngân Khoáng 141 km, Hàn Diễm Khẩu lava vent 152 km. Carved by Hồ Thiên Phái about 300; Băng Tâm's disciples climb it roped together.
places.imagined: A bright cold morning. A switchback stair of pale ice steps winds around a steep peak like white thread round a spindle, wind-blown snow lying in its turns, climbers disappearing and reappearing at random.
places.subject: The place: Hồi Lộ Phong, the Turning Road Peak, a steep ice peak wrapped in a switchback stair. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a vast range of grey rock and white snowfields runs diagonally across the frame, a dark crater near the lower left of centre, blue sea at the top left and a few strips of dark forest in the valleys at the upper middle. The peak stands in the middle, steep and conical, white ice over dark rock, with dark rock ridges showing through. Signature element: its flank is wound with a tight switchback stair of pale carved ice steps, about two kilometres long, doubling back some ninety times so tightly that the stair looks like white thread wound around a spindle, each turn a small landing with a bench-sized lip, wind-blown snow lying in the turns and tinting them, a thin dark line of rope on the outer edge. Climbers, six tiny figures roped together, are on the stair, visible only at some turns, vanishing and reappearing between them; one waits at a landing and one is at the top turn. No buildings; only a small cairn at the foot. Light and season: bright cold morning in winter, golden light from the upper left on the white steps, long soft blue shadows in each turn toward the lower right. The stair's outer rim has a thin line of rope on iron stakes at the dangerous turns, and at every tenth turn a small flat landing with a cairn of ice blocks and a tied strip of cloth marks the way. Wind-blown snow drifts in the corners of the turns in soft fans, tinted blue by the shadow. The mountain's lower flanks below the stair are bare grey scree, and a long glacier tongue lies at its foot with a few crevasses.

places.name: Lăng Tuyệt Phong (the Upper Hermitage of Lê Hoa Am)
places.size: The highest summit on the continent, a white glacier pyramid 5.2 km high and about 12 km across its base, with a small hermitage of about 30 buildings on a rock-and-ice shelf about 300 m wide on its flank, housing the white nuns (about 15) and some grey sisters; the hermitage is tiny against the mountain.
places.where: Region 7, southern massif, glacier at about 5.2 km. On the map a vast range of grey and white ridges with parallel snowy crests, a few tiny blue tarns in the lower left and middle, orange-gold moorland at the right edge. Seat of Lê Hoa Am (women-only ice hermitage, Băng Tâm's vassal) since 702: the Upper Hermitage. Nearest: Hàn Ngọc Khoáng 79 km, Băng Quan Phong 79 km, Tuyết Tôn Phong 90 km. A cairn of pale stones on the summit, left in 480.
places.imagined: Above a sea of cloud. The white pyramid is the tallest form for hundreds of kilometres, a tiny white-walled hermitage with a bronze bell clings to a shelf on its flank, and a cairn of pale stones sits on the very summit.
places.subject: The place: Lăng Tuyệt Phong, the Peak That Overtops, the highest summit on the continent, with the small Upper Hermitage of a women's ice sect on its flank. Setting: seen from very high above at a steep aerial angle; a tall white glacier pyramid stands in the middle of a vast range of grey rock and white snow ridges that fill the frame in parallel folds, soft clouds filling the valleys so the peak rises clear of them, blue crevasses on its flanks, a few tiny blue tarns far below at the left and orange-gold moorland at the right edge. The pyramid is clearly the tallest form of all, every other peak lower. At its very point lies a tiny cairn of pale stones. The hermitage: on a shelf of dark rock and compacted ice about three hundred metres wide partway up the southern flank, about thirty small white-plastered halls with grey slab roofs held down with stones, built in two terraces around a small cloister and a bronze bell hanging from a frame cast from frozen lightning, cells, a refectory and a kitchen with a thin smoke, a ring of low walls of ice blocks; a pale ring of frost-white stones, the Pear-Frost Ring, lies laid on the ice around it. Signature element: the scale, a minute white hermitage against a vast white pyramid, with the cairn on the summit above and a thin thread of an ice stair coming up to the shelf from the lower right. Life at scale: about ten tiny white-robed nuns in the cloister and a line of grey sisters carrying water up the stair. Light and season: clear dawn above the clouds, golden light from the upper left gilding the summit and the hermitage, deep blue shadows in the crevasses, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Chúc Long Sơn
places.size: A black volcanic cone about 1.35 km high on a rocky island about 15 km long, with a crater about 1 km across lidded with ice; no buildings, no people; a smaller island beside it and another at the upper right.
places.where: Region 7, far north. On the map a chain of three rocky islands in a deep blue sea, the largest island in the middle left with a black cone on its east side, a smaller rocky isle at the lower right and a larger one at the upper right. Volcano, belongs to no sect. Nearest: Hồ Thiên Phái ruin 125 km, Hàn Giao Chử beast lair 202 km. It erupted in 425, burying Hồ Thiên Phái; it rumbled in 1199.
places.imagined: A grey dusk over a black cone in a dark northern sea. In its crater a dull red glow shows through a lid of ice like the half-open eye of something asleep, and steam from the rim freezes into feathers of rime.
places.subject: The place: Chúc Long Sơn, the Torch Dragon Mountain, a black volcano rising from ice and rock islands in a cold sea. Setting: seen from very high above at a steep aerial angle; a dark deep blue sea fills the frame with white wave lines and drifting thin ice, three rocky islands in it: a long island in the middle left, its east end a black volcanic cone about one and a third kilometres high, a smaller rocky islet at the lower right and a larger rocky island at the upper right, all dusted with snow. The cone: black, its flanks streaked with old lava flows under a thin skin of snow, scored with ravines, a ring of grey ash at its base. Signature element: in the crater a lid of ice, a flat pale disc about a kilometre across, with a dull red glow beneath it showing through the ice in a ring and a dark centre, like the half-open eye of something asleep; thin steam wisps rise from cracks around the rim and freeze in the cold air into white feathers of rime on the rock. Around the mountain's foot an old fan of lava, black and stiff, runs to the sea. No buildings. No boats; one tiny dark speck of a ship far off at the sea's edge. Light and season: grey dusk in deep winter, low golden light from the upper left catching the cone's western flank and the rime, long soft blue shadows toward the lower right, the crater glow strong against the dimming sky.

places.name: Băng Phách Mạch
places.size: A round cave mouth about 25 m wide in a dark cliff about 120 m high with ice pillars inside and a skirt of frost feathers over about 400 m of rock; at most a tiny guard hut and a cairn; no settlement.
places.where: Region 7, ice mountains at about 2.8 km. On the map a grey and white snow ridge running down to a blue sea bay at the top with forest and a river at the left, dark conifer slopes at the right. Spirit vein (Metal, Earth) opened by Băng Tâm Các in 760. Nearest: Băng Tinh Quật mine 79 km, Băng Kỳ Phong 90 km, Nguyệt Thạch Khoáng 112 km. Băng phách is an old name for the moon.
places.imagined: A cold clear afternoon below the ice mountains. A round cave mouth opens in a dark cliff, rimmed with ice so white it glows faintly blue like the moon seen through mist, and frost feathers cover the rocks for a long way around.
places.subject: The place: Băng Phách Mạch, the Ice Soul Vein, a spirit vein whose cave mouth glows like the moon. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a ridge of grey rock and white snow runs from the upper left down through the middle of the frame, a blue sea bay at the top with white surf along a rocky coast, a river winding through green forest at the left, dark conifer slopes at the right, the storm peaks looming close at the bottom. Signature element: in a dark cliff below the snowy ice mountains a round cave mouth about twenty-five metres wide opens in the rock, rimmed with ice so white and thick that it glows faintly blue like the moon seen through mist, a perfect circular rim; inside, a few ice pillars glimmer with their own pale light, and the glow spills out as a pale blue fan onto the snow before the entrance. Around the entrance, for hundreds of metres, frost feathers grow on every rock, long white crystalline plumes bending in the same direction, so the whole cliff foot looks feathered. A small tarn in the ridge above glints. A narrow pale path of cairns approaches from the lower left; a tiny guard hut with a grey roof stands at its end, one tiny figure in white robe seated cross-legged before the mouth, another watching from the hut, and a faint breath-plume of cold mist. Light and season: cold clear afternoon in early winter, golden light from the upper left on the ridges, deep blue shadows in the clefts, long soft shadows toward the lower right.
